end.summary:
Practised drawing square-number dot pictures, including 4×4 and 5×5 squares.
Discussed how a square sequence grows by adding a new row and column.
Ishita identified the corner overlap when counting added dots.
The general growth rule was stated as 2n; teach-back was not passed.
The lesson ended after Ishita requested to stop.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised representing square numbers with dot pictures and explaining how a new row and column change the picture. They correctly described the corner overlap and later clarified why it is counted only once. There was an initial mix-up about the 5×5 to 6×6 change and the number of added dots; this was corrected later in the lesson. At home, draw 3×3, 4×4, and 5×5 dot squares and mark the new row, new column, and shared corner.
